name: Express Entry — Federal Skilled Worker Program (FSWP)

selection_odds.basis: Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) points-based pool; no general (all-program) draws held in 2026 to date — candidates reached primarily through category-based draws

requirements.blocker_text: This requires at least 1 year of continuous full-time skilled work experience (NOC TEER 0/1/2/3) within the last 10 years.
This requires language ability of at least CLB 7 in an official language.
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved language test at CLB 7.

requirements.blocker_text: This requires a Comprehensive Ranking System (CRS) score sufficient to receive an Invitation to Apply — in 2026, FSWP candidates are reached almost exclusively via category-based draws (e.g. French-language, healthcare, STEM, trades, education) rather than general draws, since no general draw has been held in 2026 to date.
requirements.fix_path: Improve CRS-scoring factors (age, education, language, work experience) or target a category-based draw the profile matches.

evidence_required.document: Educational Credential Assessment (ECA) if the degree was obtained abroad
Approved language test result at CLB 7

notes: MAJOR STRUCTURAL FINDING confirmed for 2026: Express Entry has held NO general (all-program) draws in 2026 to date — every 2026 round has been either program-specific (CEC, PNP) or category-based. This means pure FSWP candidates without a category-based-draw-matching profile face a genuinely uncertain path, since the traditional 'just accumulate CRS points and wait for a general draw' strategy currently has no live mechanism to act on. Direct-to-PR on approval, same structural pattern as ca_express_entry_cec and ca_express_entry_fstp — all three Express Entry programs share this direct-to-PR feature, distinct from the more common temporary-then-PR staging seen throughout the European countries in this dataset. citizenship_after_months (36) uses Canada's physical-presence formula: 1,095 days within the 5 years before applying, with pre-PR days counting as half-days up to a 365-day maximum credit — the 36-month figure is the minimum theoretical case with maximum pre-PR credit applied; realistic timelines are often longer.
